reviews.body:
hey, thanks for this one! root cause is right, and it also fixes `themeData` not showing up on first mount which was broken on main too

few things before we can merge:

- [ ] the test doesnt really prove the fix. the `themeData` in it (`{ c0: { p: ... } }`) is slot format, so `setThemeData` returns `false` and nothing actually gets themed, but the spy check still passes. use a rules theme like `{"rules":[{"id":"c0","type":"Color","value":[1,0,1]}]}` and check that `setThemeData` really returned `true` after the second load (it's a promise on the worker so await it there)
- [ ] the `load` listener is added in a `useEffect(..., [])` so it only ever attaches to the first instance. if the canvas ref detaches and reattaches (e.g a Suspense re-suspend) `setCanvasRef` creates a new instance and the listener is still sitting on the destroyed one, so the theme is gone for good after that. better to add the listener in `setCanvasRef` right where the instance is created
- [ ] when both `themeId` and `themeData` are passed the result flips now.. with `themeId="dark"` + `themeData` it renders dark, then after a `src` change it renders the `themeData` one while `activeThemeId` still says `dark`. simplest is to only re-apply on load when `themeId` isnt set

there's also still a rare unthemed frame right after a reload, but thats a core thing on our side, not blocking this PR

Updated the regression to use the rules theme and await a successful setter result after both the initial load and the reload. The load listener is now attached in setCanvasRef when each instance is created and skips restoration when themeId is configured. Added a regression for themeId priority on reload. Both tests pass on the sync and worker players; with the fix reverted, the src-change test fails on both.
